summary: This bill limits Social Security and Medicare benefits to U.S. citizens, nationals, and lawful permanent residents by narrowing eligibility rules in the Social Security Act and extending FICA taxes to previously exempt workers.

scores.thoughts: The bill restricts Medicare eligibility (section 2) and Social Security benefits (section 3) to only U.S. citizens/nationals and lawful permanent residents. This directly reduces the pool of beneficiaries and therefore reduces federal outlays on these major entitlement programs.

Section 4 amends the Internal Revenue Code to expand the FICA tax base by striking certain exemptions (paragraphs (1), (18), and (19) of section 3121(b)). This increases payroll tax collections on additional categories of remuneration.
The legislation narrows Medicare eligibility, thereby limiting access to a major public health insurance program. This has a moderate effect in the direction of restricting public coverage.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms, background checks, or gun regulations.

By explicitly limiting Social Security and Medicare benefits to citizens/nationals and lawful permanent residents only, the bill withholds benefits from other non-citizens, reinforcing a more restrictive stance on immigrant access to public programs.
No provisions address reproductive health services or abortion access.
No provisions relate to defense spending, military programs, or national security appropriations.
The bill does not address environmental regulations, climate policy, or energy production.
Sections 2 and 3 directly curtail eligibility for Social Security and Medicare, two core components of the federal social safety net, thereby scaling back benefits for non-qualifying individuals.
No provisions concern schools, student aid, or education policy.
No provisions address controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
No provisions address sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
By reducing eligibility for major entitlement programs, the bill lowers projected federal spending and thereby supports efforts to reduce deficits and the national debt.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No provisions address foreign assistance or international aid programs.
No provisions address voting access, voter ID, or election administration.
No provisions address technology regulation, data privacy, or digital oversight.
No provisions address collective bargaining, union rights, or workplace protections.
No provisions address religious exemptions or anti-discrimination rules.
